title: App Service .NET 6.0 isolated stack is past end of support
summary: Azure App Service follows the community support timeline for each language stack, and the .NET isolated stack tracks the .NET release it hosts: past its end-of-support date the app keeps running, but the platform stops providing security patches or related support for that runtime version. The .NET support policy ended support for .NET 6 on 2024-11-12, so a DOTNET-ISOLATED|6.0 app no longer receives a patched runtime.

sources.title: Language Runtime Support Policy - Azure App Service

constraints: App Service follows the community end-of-support date for each language stack and stops providing security patches and related support for that runtime version past the date.
The platform controls the minor and patch version of a managed stack, so raising the stack version is the only way to get a patched runtime.
The stack is declared in siteConfig.linuxFxVersion on Linux and siteConfig.windowsFxVersion on Windows; both are set with az webapp config set.

steps.title: Raise the App Service language stack
steps.instructions: Set dotnet-isolated to a supported stack version (see the replacement) with az webapp config set --linux-fx-version or --windows-fx-version, then redeploy the app.

steps.title: Align the stack declaration
steps.instructions: Change the same stack in the deployment source too - the siteConfig resource in an Azure Resource Manager template, the azurerm_linux_web_app linux_fx_version or azurerm_windows_web_app windows_fx_version in Terraform, and the Bicep equivalent - so the next deployment does not reset dotnet-isolated.

verification.purpose: Confirm the app reports the new stack version.

verification.command: az webapp restart --resource-group <group> --name <app> && az webapp log tail --resource-group <group> --name <app>
verification.purpose: Restart the app and watch the startup log for runtime errors on the new stack.
